name: Bootstrapping Domain Evals Without Public Benchmarks
claim_sentence: Public benchmarks do not measure a team's own task, so teams must build their own evals, often constructing the answer first or mining historical failures, because an agent you cannot evaluate is an agent you cannot improve.
definition: Speakers built evals from what they already knew: a question generated from a known source page, a contract clause that breaks a known rule, a catalog of historical bug-causing changes, a 200-question hand-built search benchmark, SME suites with a baseline, and behavior specs that grade any trajectory without ground truth. Exa's point-in-time search lets prediction features be backtested without leakage. Evaluating many drafts per task and judging with a different model family were used to control variance and self-preference. The counter-position is about the grader: LLM-as-judge verdicts proved too noisy or unstable for some teams to rely on.

name: Self-Improving Agents and Agent Management
claim_sentence: The engineer's job is shifting from writing features to managing fleets of agents and the loop that improves them: traces are centralized, scored, and turned into skill and context changes that compound.
definition: Warp, Arize, Ryan Carson, GEICO, Anthropic and Linear each described the same loop: keep receipts of every agent run, score them against rubrics, have an agent find the common failures and open PRs against the skills, and distill human review corrections back into agents.md. Engineers own the system that builds, evaluates, ships and monitors, and spin up as many agents as the merge queue allows. Business users can correct agents directly while engineering ships the change as a versioned skill. The counter-position is that the outer loop of human decisions has not kept pace, and that pushing skill and process design onto users creates competency gaps.

name: The Diffusion Gap
claim_sentence: Model capability has outrun adoption: outside coding, agents barely reach real enterprise work, and the bottleneck is process, trust and setup friction rather than intelligence.
definition: Tenex reported general-purpose LLMs in about 90 percent of large enterprises but agents in non-engineering work at about 5 percent. Anthropic said capability is no longer the constraint in financial services; Apollo called finance early; Basis said coding-style agent products push process design onto users; GEICO said the outer loop of decisions has not kept pace; Featherless traced rising token spend without productivity to process bottlenecks; and agent payment protocols see negligible volume because friction at every funnel stage suppresses demand. The counter-evidence is concrete production wins: Apollo's automated reconciliation and portfolio construction, and GEICO's one-day war room outcomes.
also_called: enterprise agents are at day one

name: Token Economics and Multi-Model Routing
claim_sentence: Production AI cost is controlled by measuring spend per use case and matching each task to the cheapest, fastest model and serving configuration that passes its evals, not by defaulting to the frontier model.
definition: Featherless, Runpod, Greptile, Ramp, GEICO, Towards AI and Exa each showed a cost lever below the model choice: per-team API keys to see spend, fast cheap models to drive adoption, batching background work, tuning vLLM against measured latency, reserving frontier models for critical steps, cheap open-weight swarms, precomputed KV-cache cartridges, many cheap drafts merged by a stronger model, and returning only relevant snippets to cut downstream tokens. The qualification is that naive turn-by-turn routing across many models destroys cache hit rates.

name: Verification Loops Over Human Review
claim_sentence: Because agents now produce code and work faster than people can read it, trust has to come from independent, deterministic verification loops that prove each outcome with evidence, not from humans reviewing every line.
definition: Speakers from software factories, code review, and agent-fleet management agreed that line-by-line human review no longer scales with agent output. They replaced it with runnable verifiers: app-specific scripts, layered zero-trust checks inside every loop, a reviewer of a different model family, and agents that exercise changes like a user and hand back screenshots, videos and test results. With verifiers in place, the verification harness becomes the durable asset and confidence becomes the product. The counter-position is that some human step stays irreducible: watching the feature video or approving an action before it lands.

name: Bounded Autonomy
claim_sentence: Agents become trustworthy the way organizations already trust non-deterministic people: through declared permissions, written policy, risk-tiered review and opinionated process, not by locking them down or approving every action.
definition: Two Sigma composes an automatic agent registry, risk-tiered review, declared tool entitlements enforced at runtime and classifiers that escalate only ambiguous calls. Coinbase treats written policy as the institution's original system prompt and places agents inside gated workflow DAGs. Basis encodes opinionated processes as behavior specs because customers value predictability over novelty, and Anthropic scopes agents with identity and least privilege. The counter-position: procedures, warnings and approvers can all be in place and still fail, and command allow-lists do not bound a compromised model.
also_called: policy as the original system prompt

name: Provenance and Grounding in Financial AI
claim_sentence: In finance, an agent earns a role in real decisions only when it runs on the firm's own governed, time-scoped data with a validated golden source, because the data and its connectors matter more than the model.
definition: Bridgewater, Apollo, Exa, Coatue and Anthropic's financial-services team all located the hard problem below the model: cleaning and aligning unstructured data to the firm's ontology, finding the golden source among many, giving agents direct access to every source a human sees through one connectivity layer, and serving the web as it looked on a past date so a backtest cannot see the future. A generic web-searching agent answering from one stale source was the cautionary example.
why_uncontested: No speaker argued that a general-purpose model without the firm's own governed data could carry a trading or investment decision; Apollo grants general LLMs only a research role, which restates the theme rather than opposing it.

name: The Sandboxed Computer and Evolving Harness
claim_sentence: Agent harnesses are converging on a separate, disposable sandboxed computer as the execution boundary, while the prompt scaffolding they once added is being absorbed into the models.
definition: Every agent framework, however much they disagree, integrates the same create-run-delete sandbox primitives, because allow-lists and embedded runtimes do not bound a compromised model and a throwaway VM does. Greptile, Arize and Ryan Carson run their agents in cloud sandboxes for the same reason, and that boundary must be chosen before the framework. Meanwhile the harness's intelligence tricks are being learned by the models through a data flywheel, so harnesses should ship and unship features easily. The counter-position, from the same talks, is that the harness keeps infrastructure, trust and efficiency, and must re-add prompting and guardrails in every new domain.

name: Owning Open Foundations vs. Renting the Frontier
claim_sentence: Companies should own their agent stack on open, model-swappable foundations rather than rent it from frontier labs, because models are commoditizing and the labs will recoup their spend by locking customers in or competing with them.
definition: Nous Research made the case most directly: frontier models are interchangeable, so labs move up to the agent layer and into lucrative domains, and whatever platform a company roots its agentic processes in hardens into its organization. Ramp, Daytona and Arize argued the practical half: go a layer below the frontier APIs, use open-weight models where they keep most of the quality, and keep the harness model-agnostic so models can be swapped. The counter-position is that frontier capability already outpaces adoption and keeps getting cheaper, so building on a lab's foundation, or simply waiting, is the rational move.
also_called: go a layer below the frontier

name: The Context Problem
claim_sentence: Once code is cheap, agents fail for lack of intent, history and tribal knowledge rather than intelligence, so teams must build systems that assemble that context before and around the agent.
definition: At Linear, agents read the code yet miss intent, prior decisions, owners and recent reverts, so a triage agent enriches each issue and a context-aware reviewer catches product-level mistakes. GEICO found that synthesized context and the right decision makers, not coding speed, rate-limited legacy modernization, and that once context was built a cheaper model wrote as well as the frontier. Greptile replaces imprecise RAG with a maintained codebase wiki; Ramp precomputes predictable context into KV-cache cartridges. The counter-position is the data flywheel: what the harness supplies today the model learns natively tomorrow.

name: Spatiotemporal World Models and Simulation
claim_sentence: Models trained to predict video frames and actions at scale will learn physics and real-time control, becoming simulators and agents that act in space and time rather than in turns of text.
definition: General Intuition and Runway both bet on scaling laws for video: General Intuition on action-labeled gameplay that maps onto robot teleoperation, Runway on next-frame prediction that learns gravity, occlusion and object permanence and can render an interactive interface with no 3D engine. Both expect the result to unlock robotics and new businesses. They differ on supervision: General Intuition argues explicit action labels transfer better than inferred ones.
